message:
How it reads now:
Contracts sheet
Customer (text, required), Value a year (money, required), Start (date), Renews on (date), Notice (days), Owner (person, whoever adds it), Budget owner (person), Billing email (email), Customer contact (text).
The form: Basics (Customer, Value a year, Owner, Budget owner, Billing email and Customer contact), Dates (Start, Renews on and Notice). Asked when creating: Customer and Value a year.

Steps
Draft → Legal review, for contracts over $50,000 → Signed → Active → Renewal due → Renewed or Ended

What happens by itself
60 days before a contract's notice date, if it is still Active, move it to Renewal due and email its owner to ask them to act on the renewal.
30 days before a contract's notice date, if it is still in Renewal due, email Wade and the owner to tell them nobody has acted.
When a contract enters Renewal due, start a request in Renewal requests in Spend, named after the customer, with the customer, the yearly value, the renewal date and the contract's budget owner.

Who can see and do what
Wade Wilson and Krishna see every contract, add, edit and move them, and change how it works.
Contract owners see their own contracts and can edit and move them.
Everyone else sees nothing.

Connections
People fills Owner.
People fills Budget owner.
At Renewal due, start a renewal request in Spend.

Coming soon
Connections to other software

Latest message from Wade Wilson:
Remind owners 90 days before the notice date instead of 60.
